note: The input codepoint stream (62 LREs and one RLE that raise the embedding level to 125, followed by '[' LRI PDI '(' PDF RLE ']') is run-length encoded into the run list that later gets corrupted.

Every run records its isolate level here. The LRI run at pos 64 keeps isolate_level 0; the overflown isolate increments the counter so the following PDI run at pos 65 gets isolate_level 1, while both remain at embedding level 125.

Isolate chains are built per isolate level in list order: the '[' run (R5), the LRI run (R6) and the ']' run (R11) form the iso-0 chain, while the PDI run (R7) and the '(' run (R8) form the iso-1 chain.

The merge predicate compares embedding levels and neutrality but never compares RL_ISOLATE_LEVEL, so the adjacent neutral runs R6 (iso 0) and R7 (iso 1) at the same level 125 satisfy it and R7 is merged into R6 even though they belong to different isolate sequences.

Merging R7 into R6 (different isolate levels) overwrites R6's isolate-chain successor with R7's successor R8, while R11->prev_isolate still points back to R6; the isolate-chain links are now corrupted.
The second compaction pass (after bracket properties are cleared at line 1214) merges R6 into R5 and then R8 into R5, freeing R6; R11->prev_isolate now dangles to the freed R6.
Merging R11 into R5 (same type and level) writes through R11->prev_isolate, which still points to the already freed R6 run; this is the use-after-free write performed by the later compaction merge.
